title: The は particle
summary: は is not a carriage. It is a flag that says what the sentence is about, and it never changes who does what.

blocks.text: Many courses teach **は** on day one, so learners think it means "is" or "the subject". It is neither. は (read "wa" when it is a particle) can never be a main carriage, and it is not a white carriage like を. It is a **flag** that you plant on the **topic**: what the sentence is about. It does not say anything about the topic; the real sentence does that.
Because は is not a logical particle, the sentence underneath still needs its own main carriage and が (often a zero).
私は学生だ。 Literally: "As for me, (I) am a student."

A famous puzzle: 「私はうなぎだ」 does **not** mean "I am an eel". At a restaurant the zero carriage is the **dish**, not the speaker: "As for me, (it) is eel," so "I'll have the eel." The topic flag shapes which zero you hear.

blocks.en: As for me, (it) is eel: I'll have the eel.

blocks.text: The logical particles decide who does what
**が** marks the doer and **を** marks what is done to.
**に** marks the **target**, the person or place the action is aimed at. Because these three fix the roles, word order is flexible. Even a silly sentence stays grammatical: the particles decide.
私がさくらにボールを投げる。

blocks.jp: 私がさくらにボールを投げる。
blocks.en: I throw the ball to Sakura.

blocks.jp: 私にさくらがボールを投げる。
blocks.en: Sakura throws the ball to me. The order changed, but the particles still say who does what.

blocks.jp: ボールがさくらを私に投げる。
blocks.en: The ball throws Sakura to me. (nonsense, but perfectly grammatical)

blocks.text: Moving は changes emphasis, never logic
Changing a logical particle changes the event. Moving the は flag only changes what you are talking about.
ボールは私がさくらに（Øを）投げる。 As for the ball, I throw (it) to Sakura.

blocks.title: The same event, three topics
rows: 私はさくらにボールを投げる。
As for me, I throw the ball to Sakura.
さくらには私がボールを投げる。
As for Sakura, I throw the ball to her.
ボールは私がさくらに投げる。
As for the ball, I throw it to Sakura.

blocks.title: Remember
items: **は** flags the **topic**. It says nothing about it.
は is not a main carriage and not a white carriage.
The sentence under the topic still has its own が, often a zero.
**が・を・に** decide who does what to whom. Moving **は** never changes that.

questions.note: は flags the topic.
questions.en: As for my older brother, (he) is a doctor.

questions.prompt: 妹は私＿＿ボールを投げる。
questions.note: に marks the target of the throw.
questions.en: My younger sister throws the ball to me.

questions.note: は plants a flag on what the sentence is about.
は only flags the topic; the engine says the real thing.

questions.instruction: Does は say anything about the topic?
options: No, the rest of the sentence does
Yes, that it is the subject
Yes, that it is a verb
questions.note: The flag only points; the sentence under it speaks.

questions.prompt: At a café your friend says: 私はコーヒーだ。
questions.note: The topic flag shapes the zero, just like the eel sentence.
questions.en: As for me, (it) is coffee: I'll have coffee.

questions.instruction: Which particle only flags the topic?
questions.note: は sets the topic; が, を and に mark roles.

questions.prompt: 子供が犬にボールを投げる。
options: 犬が子供にボールを投げる。
子供が犬をボールに投げる。
犬を子供がボールが投げる。
ボールを犬に子供が投げる。
questions.note: The particles fix the roles, so the order may change.
questions.en: The child throws the ball to the dog.

questions.prompt: 子供が犬にボールを投げる。
questions.note: に marks the target: the dog.
questions.en: The child throws the ball to the dog.

questions.prompt: ボールは私が犬に投げる。
questions.note: The は flag sits on ボール.
questions.en: As for the ball, I throw (it) to the dog.

questions.note: に says where the action is aimed.
は flags the topic.
questions.en: As for that younger brother, (he) is a student.

questions.note: が marks the main carriage, not は.
questions.en: Today my older sister reads a book.

questions.note: に marks the target of the writing.
questions.en: I write a letter to my mother.

questions.note: は flags what the sentence is about.
questions.en: As for my older brother, (he) runs every day.

questions.prompt: As for my mother, (she) is a teacher.
questions.note: Topic, noun, だ.
questions.en: As for my mother, (she) is a teacher.

questions.prompt: As for me, (I) throw the ball.
questions.note: は flag first, then を, then the verb.
questions.en: As for me, (I) throw the ball.

questions.prompt: As for my younger brother, (he) throws the ball to the dog.
questions.note: Topic, target, object, verb.
questions.en: As for my younger brother, (he) throws the ball to the dog.

questions.instruction: What happens to the logic if you move は?
questions.note: は is not a logical particle.

questions.instruction: Which sentence uses は correctly as the topic flag?
questions.note: は follows the topic and the engine closes the sentence.
questions.en: As for my younger sister, (she) is a student.

questions.note: The particles fix the roles, so the order may change.
questions.en: My older sister throws paper to me.

questions.prompt: 先生に弟がボールを投げる。
questions.note: が marks the thrower; に marks the one who gets the ball.
questions.en: My younger brother throws the ball to the teacher.

questions.prompt: As for the ball, my sister throws (it) to me.
questions.note: Topic flag first, then the doer, the target and the verb.
questions.en: As for the ball, my older sister throws (it) to me.
